title: CLI command execution and dispatch lifecycle
answers: How does control flow from Command.main to command callbacks?
What is the execution lifecycle of a Click command or group?
How are subcommands dispatched and invoked in Click?
body:
Control flow begins at `src/click/core.py:Command.main` and dispatches via:
`src/click/core.py:Command.main` → `src/click/core.py:Command.make_context` → `src/click/core.py:Context.scope` → `src/click/core.py:Command.invoke` → `src/click/core.py:Context.invoke`.
- `src/click/core.py:Command.main` parses commandline arguments (`sys.argv[1:]`) and enters `src/click/core.py:Context.scope` to manage teardown via `ExitStack`.
- `src/click/core.py:Command.invoke` parses option/argument tokens into `ctx.params` using `src/click/core.py:Parameter.handle_parse_result`.
- For groups, `src/click/core.py:Group.invoke` calls `src/click/core.py:Group.resolve_command` to locate subcommands, builds a child `Context(parent=ctx)`, and delegates execution to `subcommand.invoke`.
- `src/click/core.py:Context.invoke` unpacks parsed keyword arguments and executes the underlying command callback function.
applies: Applies to all Click command and group executions, including single commands, multi-level nested groups, and chained commands.
